title: Scripture and Tradition (Divine Revelation)
requirements: Explore how God reveals Himself through both Sacred Scripture and Sacred Tradition, the role of the Magisterium, and how the biblical canon was formed.
reading: CCC 80–100, 101–141 | Dei Verbum #9 | Scripture: 2 Thessalonians 2:15, 2 Timothy 3:16–17

sections.title: 1. Jesus as God's Ultimate Revelation
sections.content: Before discussing Scripture and Tradition, we must look at the ultimate, once-and-for-all way God revealed Himself: through Jesus Christ.
points: Jesus is the fullness of God’s Revelation to the world, revealing the Father through His life, death, and resurrection.
Jesus taught His apostles and disciples and empowered them to preach salvation to the entire world, continuing His mission through apostolic succession.

sections.title: 2. Sacred Tradition (Capital 'T')
sections.content: Catholic teaching distinguishes between small 't' traditions (like dinner prayers) and capital 'T' Tradition, which is the living transmission of the Gospel message in the Church.
points: It consists of the oral preaching of the Apostles handed down through an unbroken line of bishops (apostolic succession).
Catholics view Scripture and Tradition as one single, sacred deposit of the Word of God, equally vital to divine revelation.

sections.title: 3. The Magisterium and Authenticity
sections.content: The task of authentically interpreting the Word of God has been entrusted to the living teaching office of the Church alone (the Magisterium).

criteria.description: Was the teaching believed everywhere with universal acceptance?
Can the teaching be traced back to our earliest apostolic origins?
Has this teaching been embraced by the faithful throughout the ages?

sections.title: 4. The Biblical Canon
sections.content: The canon refers to the defined collection of 46 Old Testament and 27 New Testament books accepted as authoritative within the Church.
points: The Church did not arbitrarily create the canon; rather, it formally recognized and preserved the texts that already possessed universal authority, antiquity, and apostolic consensus.

catechism_reading.description: To dive deeper into tonight's topic, read these sections in your Catechism this week:

readings.summary: The Tradition of the Apostles and the Magisterium.
Christ as the unique Word of Sacred Scripture.

questions: How does the Catholic understanding of Scripture and Tradition working together differ from looking at the Bible alone?
Why is it significant that Jesus entrusted His revelation to a living community of apostles and disciples rather than just writing a book?

scriptural_foundations.title: Holding to Tradition
scriptural_foundations.summary: St. Paul encourages believers to stand firm and hold fast to the traditions taught whether by word of mouth or by letter.

scriptural_foundations.title: Unity of Scripture and Tradition
scriptural_foundations.summary: Both sacred Tradition and sacred Scripture are to be accepted and venerated with the same sense of loyalty and reverence.
